subject: Closure dataflow playbook — questions, constraints, and next steps

Subject: Re: Quick call on exit / deletion pathways?

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo today — helpful high level. A couple of follow ups from our legal/privacy team:

- We need a clear description of how requests to delete customer data flow through Redwood (which services touch PII).
- What is your practical SLA for complete deletion for an account vs individual records (we saw the demo purge button, but need timelines around snapshots/backups).
- Do you support a deletion certification output or evidence package for audit?
- Residency: can deleted data be guaranteed to be removed from backups/replication if we require EU-only residency?

Can you send a short playbook or checklist we can hand to our ops/legal? Also please call out any constraints — e.g., immutable snapshot retention windows, RPO windows, or third-party backup providers.

Appreciate it — Kendal(l)

Kendall — thanks for the clear list. Replied inline and attached a concise kickoff checklist (RTBF_kickstart_checklist.xlsx) that maps the items to owners/inputs and our typical timelines. High level answers below and then a couple of asks so we can finalize the playbook for your audit team.

On Fri, Oct 1, 2026 at 3:02 PM Kendall Moss <kendall@finclosure.com> wrote:
> Hi Rachel,
> 
> Thanks for the demo today — helpful high level. A couple of follow ups from our legal/privacy team:

> - We need a clear description of how requests to delete customer data flow through Redwood (which services touch PII).
> - What is your practical SLA for complete deletion for an account vs individual records (we saw the demo purge button, but need timelines around snapshots/backups).
> - Do you support a deletion certification output or evidence package for audit?
> - Residency: can deleted data be guaranteed to be removed from backups/replication if we require EU-only residency?

>

Quick answers (summary):
- Dataflow: requests hit our Control Plane (API) → queued job evaluated by Privacy Ops → serve-layer data tombstoned and KV cache invalidated → background purge process removes model inputs/outputs from active stores. Long-term snapshots and backups are handled via your configured backup retention policy and are not automatically purged immediately on request; we provide a documented process to overwrite/expire snapshots where possible.

- SLA: For account-level erase we typically commit to a 30–90 day operational completion window depending on backup cycle and whether legal holds exist. Individual-record deletes (API-level) are completed within 7–14 days in the active stores; again backups can extend that window.

- Audit evidence: yes — we can produce an evidence package (deletion summary, affected object IDs, job run logs, and a signed attestation). Ben, could you confirm the typical evidence bundle contents we provide?

- Residency & backups: If you require EU-only residency, we operate a residency-controlled region where active data and primary backups are kept in-region. Cross-region snapshots/replication can be disabled for the account. Immutable third-party backups (customer-managed) are a constraint — we will need confirmation of providers and retention windows to map the purge path.

Asks (so we tailor the playbook):
1) Which object types are in scope (conversation logs, embedding vectors, full request/response payloads, diagnostic traces)?
2) Target SLA for account-level completion that Legal will accept (30 / 60 / 90 days)?
3) Any ongoing legal holds or litigation holds we should know about?
4) Do you manage backups with a third party (vault provider / cloud snapshot tooling)? If so, provider + typical retention period?

Next steps: attaching RTBF_kickstart_checklist.xlsx — please fill columns A–C and return. I will schedule a 45-min technical deep dive with our Privacy Lead (Soojin) to walk through the snapshot chain and audit package. Proposed slots: Tue Oct 12 10:00–10:45 PDT or Wed Oct 13 14:00–14:45 PDT.

Regards,
Rachel Kim

Subject: Re: Quick call on exit / deletion pathways? — technical clarifications and evidence package

Rachel / Kendall — adding some technical detail to what I promised on the call. I attached a slightly redacted internal playbook (redwood-rtbf-playbook-v2.pdf) and a short note on snapshot semantics (snapshot-policy-notes.txt). Short answers below so Kendall can circulate to Legal/Infra: 

1) What touches PII / dataflow:
- Ingestion: API gateway + request logs (ingress) — request bodies are stored encrypted at rest for active retention period.
- Serving: model inputs/outputs live in short-term active stores (hot KV + request store) and are persisted to our primary object store per customer namespace.
- Traces/diagnostics: controlled by account debug flags; these are not collected by default.

2) Backups & snapshots:
- Primary backups: daily incremental snapshots + weekly full snapshots. We keep a snapshot chain; deleting an object triggers a tombstone in active stores and marks the object for expiry in the next snapshot rollover.
- Immutable snapshots: if your environment uses an external archival vault with immutability windows (e.g., write-once for 180 days), Redwood cannot forcibly delete that copy; we will document the location and provide an overwriting/expiry request to the vault operator.
- Practical time to remove from all copies: typical range 30–90 days depending on the oldest snapshot that contains the data and your configured retention.

3) Evidence package contents:
- Deletion job run ID(s) and timestamps
- Affected object IDs (hashes/identifiers)
- Log snippet of job steps (redacted)
- Confirmation of snapshot expiry proposal or vault operator correspondence
- Signed attestation of Redwood operator actions

4) EU residency specifics:
- We can ensure active stores + primary backups remain in eu-west-1 for your account; replication to other regions is disabled by default for residency-controlled accounts. Cross-region immutable archives need to be vetted case-by-case.

Limitations / callouts:
- If customers enable long-term immutable logging via a third-party export, those copies remain under the third-party's retention policy. We can assist with contact points and an evidence trail but do not control deletion of customer-managed immutable exports.

Attached: redwood-rtbf-playbook-v2.pdf (redacted playbook), snapshot-policy-notes.txt (policy snippets).

Ben Carter

Recap (short):
- Active-store deletion: 7–14 days for individual records, tombstone applied immediately to active namespaces.
- Account-level completion: target 30–90 days depending on snapshot/backups and legal holds.
- Snapshot/backups: daily incremental + weekly full; immutable third-party vaults may block immediate removal.
- Evidence: Redwood will produce an audit bundle (job IDs, object IDs, logs, attestation).
